source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio SAT5-SAT6 campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity, but the disclosure stops there: no power source, no grid details, no evidence any of it serves AI.

The campus ranks sixth among the nineteen Texas facilities that publish power capacity, which works out to 6.9% of the state's disclosed total of 475 MW. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, so that ranking measures how many operators disclose, not how much capacity the state actually holds. Nineteen out of 133 is a disclosure rate, and any state total assembled from it is a floor rather than a census.

The certifications are HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type 2, TIA-942, and HITRUST. They qualify the site for regulated enterprise, healthcare, and federal workloads, which is hygiene for that customer base and not a marker of AI use. A campus built for compliance-heavy tenants may run at densities well below what accelerator racks require, and the operator publishes neither rack density nor accelerator count. Applying 40 kW per rack to 33 MW yields roughly 825 racks, but that is an assumption laid over the number, not a fact the operator states.

What the data does not cover is the part that matters for AI scaling: grid interconnection, power source, whether the 33 MW is contracted, allocated, or available, and whether any workload on site is training. Without those, this facility cannot be placed on the compute-to-power chain. It is one disclosed capacity figure in a state where most facilities disclose nothing at all.
